THE WICKED AND THE HOLY — COMPLETE TEXT

FRAGMENT 1 — THE AGES AND THE WATCHERS — 4Q181 Fragment 1

1 [Interpretation concerning the ages which The Creator made:] An age of wickedness for [seventy] weeks. And they became defiled in it. The angels of Mastemah walked in it and the children of men forgot the covenant of YHWH.

2 And YHWH spoke to the Watchers of heaven and commanded them: Do not look upon the daughters of men. But they transgressed His word. They descended and they took wives from among the daughters of men and they corrupted the earth.

3 Therefore YHWH appointed judgment against them. Their sons — the Nephilim — were destroyed in the flood. And the Watchers themselves were bound in the places of darkness beneath the earth, reserved for the judgment of the great day.

4 But from among the children of men YHWH chose for Himself a remnant who had not defiled themselves with the corruption of the Watchers. From this remnant He raised up the covenant people and preserved the seed of righteousness through the flood.

5 And YHWH said: the wicked are appointed for darkness and the holy are appointed for light. This appointment was made before the foundation of the earth. It is not changed by the deeds of men but confirmed by them.

6 Therefore let the holy ones walk in confidence. Their inheritance was determined before they were born. Their names are written in the book of life and the glory of YHWH will be their covering in the day of judgment.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 4Q181 is a companion to 4Q180 (Ages of Creation) and both interpret the Watcher tradition of Chanokh within a periodized history framework. The binding of the Watchers beneath the earth is consistent with Chanokh 10 in the Orit Ge'ez version. This confirms that the 4Q181 author drew on the same ancient Chanokh tradition preserved in the Ge'ez canon.

[ORIT GE'EZ] The Orit Ge'ez Chanokh 10:4-14 describes the binding of the Watchers in detail: Aza'el is bound hand and foot and cast into darkness until the day of judgment. The Wicked and the Holy text confirms this tradition in Hebrew, demonstrating that the Ge'ez version of the Watcher-judgment narrative is not a late development but an ancient tradition with Hebrew attestation at Qumran.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] The Masoretic Bereshit 6:1-4 contains only a brief and cryptic reference to the sons of God taking human wives and the Nephilim resulting. The Masoretic tradition suppresses the full Watcher narrative. The Qumran texts — including the Wicked and the Holy — preserve the fuller ancient tradition that the Masoretic canonical process reduced to an unexplained four-verse fragment.

[CRITICAL NOTE] The statement that the holy ones' appointment was determined before the foundation of the earth is a doctrine of pre-temporal election. This concept — that the righteous were chosen before creation — predates and is independent of any Christian theological development of predestination. It is an ancient Hebrew theological concept rooted in the divine council tradition: YHWH's decisions about human destiny precede the creation they govern.
